newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.400 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

The sharp discount October holds to the CME lean hog index after August expired on Thursday combined with technical strength should support hog futures early. Steady to higher cash hog indications on increased packer interest for a Saturday kill also was seen supportive, analysts said.
However, the market could be overbought after recent gains and could slip ahead of the weekend, they added.

Further strength in pork belly futures was expected, linked to a strong tone to cash belly prices as prices rebounded somewhat this week after last week's slide, and continued lack of deliveries against futures. August deliverable stocks remain in strong hands, analysts noted.
USDA quoted 14-16 lb fresh bellies at $80 to $82 per cwt Thursday, up $1 to $2, and up from $78 early in the week.
Back months may also climb based on technical strength. February broke through chart resistance at 74.200 cents on Thursday's climb, sources said.
